text.p: Anheuser-Busch Cos. Inc., the No. 1 U.S. brewer, reported a record annual profit of $1.16 billion and record sales Wednesday.
The St. Louis-based company, which brews Budweiser and Michelob beer, had 1996 net income equivalent to $2.28 a share, compared with $886.6 million, or $1.72 a share, in 1995.
Revenues rose to $12.6 billion from $12 billion a year ago.

For the fourth quarter, the company had net income of $150 million, or 30 cents a share, on revenues of $2.89 billion, compared with a loss of $8.9 million, or 1 cent a share, on revenues of $2.6 billion in the same period a year ago.
Earnings for the quarter and the year were in line with analyst expectations.
Anheuser-Busch stock rose $1 to $43.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Anheuser-Busch also said it sold a record 91.1 million barrels of beer last year, a 4.1 increase from 1995.
The company boosted its dominant domestic market share by 1.1 percentage points to 45.2 percent.
Anheuser-Busch Chief Financial Officer W. Randolph Baker said in an interview that the company continued to aim for a double-digit percentage increase in earnings this year.
"As we end 1996 and begin 1997, we do so in a position of great competitive strength and we have set the stage for significant long-term earnings growth for 1997, Baker said.

The 1996 results included a $54.7 million gain on the sale of the St. Louis Cardinals professional baseball team and the team's stadium, but excluded $33.8 million in income from discontinued operations.
The 1995 figures included the $160 million cost of closing the company's brewery in Tampa, Fla., but excluded a loss of $244.3 million from discontinued operations.
